Jasmine —

Quick technical notes to include in the consolidated response: these are targeted to Hestia's specific asks. Feel free to paste/quote as-is.

1) Telemetry sampling and availability windows- We collect per-request health and latency metrics at the ingress proxy layer at 1-second granularity, roll those metrics into 1-minute buckets per endpoint instance, and then compute availability on 5-minute sliding windows where a window is "available" if at least one successful request completes within the window. This approach tolerates brief transient spikes while still capturing meaningful outages.

2) Latency definition - Latency reported = server-side request-to-last-token completion time ( excludes client-side sequencing/processing). We report rolling p95 and p99 over 24-hour intervals. For streamed responses we measure time to first token (TTFT) and time-to-last-token separately; credits reference time-to-last-token unless parties agree otherwise.

3) Sampling/weighting and regional aggregation- Metrics are aggregated per-region (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and weighted by received request counts. For multi-region customers we compute a regionally weighted availability figure as the denominator for credits, unless the customer elects per-region SLAs.

4) Service credit proposal (example table)
- Availability >= 99.95%: 0% credit
- 99.90% — 99.95%: 5% of monthly invoice
- 99.75% — 99.90%: 10% of monthly invoice
- 99.50% — 99.75%: 20% of monthly invoice
- < 99.50%: 25% of monthly invoice (monthly cap)

Notes on calculation: credits are prorated based on the worst-performing region unless a per-region SLA is contracted. Maintenance windows (scheduled) are excluded if communicated 48 hours in advance and published in the scheduled maintenance calendar.

5) Evidence and dispute process- For any disputed window we will provide raw 1-minute bucket telemetry and request traces (P95 sample set) for the disputed period. Disputes must be raised within 15 calendar days of the monthly statement.

I'll also flag that our observability team can run a one-month synthetic probe alongside Hestia's tests as a neutral signal for acceptance testing.

Marcus Lin

Thanks — a few legal-side redlines and recommendations: 

1) Monthly cap: move to 15% as a starting position in the MSA but offer 25% if Hestia signs a 12-month committed Dedicated capacity agreement. That gives negotiation leverage.

2) Exclusions: expand to include third-party cloud provider outages (e.g., region-level provider incidents) where vendor posts an incident; include customer misconfiguration where evidence shows requests failed after our ingress.

3) Notice periods: scheduled maintenance excluded if 48 hours published notice and windows are limited to a combined 6 hours per month (we can agree to longer for major upgrades with added notice).

4) Measurement methodology clause: keep the product description Marcus wrote but add the following sentence — "Customer acknowledges that server-side telemetry is the measurement of record for purposes of calculating Availability and Latency SLOs."

5) Dispute resolution: disputes to be escalated to our SRE leads with 10 business days for joint analysis, binding arbitration only as last resort.

I'll generate a redlined PDF and attach. Recommend we present an initial offer 15% cap and the product team to provide a companion note proposing observability playbook (synthetic probes + customer probes) to reduce ambiguity.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
